claim: ANO1 currents exhibit robust anion:cation selectivity (PNa/PCl = 0.03).

claim: The ANO6 current is highly non-selective.
source: In comparison to ANO1 currents, which exhibit robust anion:cation selectivity (PNa/PCl = 0.03), the ANO6 current is highly non-selective (Figure 5).
evidence: This claim is supported by ionic selectivity measurements shown in Figure 5.

claim: The ionic selectivity sequence of ANO6 was Na+ > Cl− > Cs+ > NMDG+ (PNa/PCl = 1.38, PCs/PCl = 0.6, PNMDG/PCl = 0.48).
source: The ionic selectivity sequence was Na+ > Cl− > Cs+ > NMDG+ (PNa/PCl = 1.38, PCs/PCl = 0.6, PNMDG/PCl = 0.48).

claim: The finding that ANO6 currents have very low ionic selectivity and are activated contemporaneously with PLS over the same Ca2+ concentration range suggested that PLS and currents have the same underlying mechanism.

claim: ANO6 contains a domain responsible for PLS that is absent in ANO1.

claim: There are three major regions of Type-II divergence between ANO1 and ANO6.
source: There are three major regions of Type-II divergence between ANO1 and ANO 6 (Figure 6A).

claim: The three major regions of Type-II divergence between ANO1 and ANO6 are located in (a) intracellular loop 1, (b) TMD4 and TMD5 and the short intracellular loop between them, and (c) the C-terminus adjacent to the last transmembrane domain.
source: These regions are located in (a) intracellular loop 1, (b) TMD4 and TMD5 and the short intracellular loop between them, and (c) the C-terminus adjacent to the last transmembrane domain.
evidence: This claim is supported by computational analysis shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Of 26 1-6-1 chimeras, 17 trafficked to the plasma membrane and generated Cl− currents in patch clamp.

claim: 13 1-6-1 chimeras did not exhibit PLS.
source: 13 1-6-1 chimeras did not exhibit PLS.

claim: The fungal ANO homolog nhTMEM16 exhibits PLS activity when reconstituted into liposomes.

source: Brunner et al. speculate that this region may be involved in lipid transport.
